newsitem.title: MONACO: OLYMPICS-SAMARANCH UNHAPPY WITH BED TAX FOR SYDNEY GAMES.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-SAMARANCH UNHAPPY WITH BED TAX FOR SYDNEY GAMES.

text.p: A new bed tax which New South Wales state government plan to impose on hoteliers in Sydney, hosts of the 2000 Olympics, has upset International Olympic Commitee president Juan Antonio Samaranch.
"We are not happy with the tax and the hotels are also not happy," Samaranch said on Thursday. "We can do nothing -- only tell the organisers that we are not happy."

The 10 percent bed tax, which was included in the state budget earlier this month, will apply from September 1 on accommodation at hotels, motels and guests houses in Sydney's central business district and is projected to raise A$64 (US$50.07) million a year.
The state wants the tax to help support the A$2.1 (US$1.64) billion of government money which will be spent on Olympic projects.
Sydney's budget and plans for the Games were well received by the IOC and international sporting federations during meetings here in the last few days.

Samaranch reacted in typically diplomatic style to a question suggesting that Australians would prefer an Australian to open the Games rather than the country's head of state, Britain's Queen Elizabeth.
"The IOC will respect the will of the people of Australia," he said.
